The test image shows a **stem** near the soil line with reddish-brown to dark brown discoloration and a sunken lesion. This narrows candidates to stem diseases: Rhizoctonia, Phytophthora, Fusarium, Charcoal_Rot, Pythium_damping_off, Brown_Stem_Rot, Anthracnose, White_Mold.

Now I'll view one reference from each top candidate.

The second Rhizoctonia reference is a near-perfect match — reddish-brown sunken canker on the lower stem near the soil line, identical coloration and location to the test image. I need one more from a new class (8 classes minimum).

Anthracnose shows extensive dark browning along the full stem, not matching the test image's localized soil-line canker.

**Summary of analysis:**

- Test image: reddish-brown to dark brown, sunken, firm lesion on the hypocotyl/lower stem at the soil line
- Rhizoctonia (Dise_36): near-perfect match — same reddish-orange to dark brown sunken canker at the soil line
- Other candidates ruled out:
  - Phytophthora: chocolate-brown extending up multiple nodes
  - Charcoal_Rot: gray with black microsclerotia specks
  - Fusarium: internal vascular discoloration, no external canker
  - Pythium: water-soaked soft rot
  - Brown_Stem_Rot: internal pith browning (needs stem split to see)
  - Anthracnose: diffuse browning along full stem with black acervuli

The reddish-brown, sunken, firm canker at the soil line is the classic diagnostic signature of Rhizoctonia.
